unit.why: A single legend about the Maharal of Prague (author of Gur Aryeh), a pre-Hasidic sage, who rescues a prodigy from priests who use teraphim; it is explicitly linked to an earlier tale about R. Pinto.

stories.start_quote: נספר בזה מעשה נורא מהגאון הקדוש
stories.summary_en: A 12-year-old prodigy in Prague is lured away by merchants posing as a rich in-law. They are really priests who want to cut off his head and use it as a teraphim oracle. An old talking head of an earlier victim helps him escape, and the Maharal's public fast, Psalms and prayer bring him home miraculously in one night. The Maharal then destroys the impure names and promises to recite kaddish for the head.
